messages.subject: measurement invariance for binary data
parts:
Hi group
first) i need some one to approve the sequence i have used in measurment invaraince for binary data. Of course, I have modified the commands of this link. second) as i find for binary data rsultes of weak and strong model have the same degree of freedom and the same results, so we just run one of them, Is this conclusion correct? third) can we ignore intercepts for analysis because they are always fixed on zero?

test.seq <- list(strong = c("thresholds","loadings","intercepts"),
                 strict = "residuals",
                 means = "means",
                 lv.variances="lv.variances")
meq.list <- list()

  if (i == 0L) {
    meq.label <- "configural"
    group.equal <- ""

                                         data = CSBD_B_G,

                                         parameterization = "theta",

                                         ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
                                         group = "Gender",

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measurement invariance for binary data
parts:
The ?measEq.syntax help-page example for binary data shows that you should compare configural to "strong" invariance.  There is no valid way to test equality of thresholds, loadings, and intercepts separately.  If strong invariance is violated, it could be due to any of those parameters, without any way for the data to tell us which.
